# apple_subscription_win_back_offer (Resource)

Manages a win-back offer: a discounted or free period the App Store offers to customers whose subscription has lapsed, shown on their Manage Subscriptions page, on the win-back offer sheet inside the app, and — if promoted — on the App Store itself.

An offer belongs to one subscription, not to the group: a customer is eligible only for offers on the product they most recently lapsed from within each group, so reaching lapsed subscribers of several plans takes one offer per plan.

~> **The subscription has to have been approved by App Review first.** Apple refuses to create a win-back offer for one that has never been approved.

~> **The prices cannot change after creation.** Apple's update request carries no prices, so every change to `prices` destroys the offer and creates a new one — and the new one cannot reuse the old `offer_id` (see below). The same is true of `reference_name`, `offer_id`, `duration`, `offer_mode`, `period_count` and `target_subscription_plan_type`. The eligibility rules, the dates, `priority` and `promotion_intent` change in place, though Apple refuses some of those changes once the offer is live.

Apple allows at most 350 win-back offers per subscription, and at most 5 running at once per storefront.

`terraform destroy` deletes the offer, which Apple allows at any time; a customer holding a link to it is told the offer is no longer available.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "apple_apps" "example" {
  bundle_id = "com.example.app"
}

data "apple_subscription_groups" "premium" {
  app_id = data.apple_apps.example.apps[0].id
}

# A win-back offer needs a subscription App Review has already approved, so it
# is usually read rather than created alongside the offer.
data "apple_subscriptions" "pro_monthly" {
  group_id           = data.apple_subscription_groups.premium.subscription_groups[0].id
  product_id_pattern = "^com\\.example\\.app\\.pro\\.monthly$"
}

# The offer price in one storefront, fanned out to every other one.
data "apple_subscription_price_points" "offer_base" {
  subscription_id = data.apple_subscriptions.pro_monthly.subscriptions[0].id
  territories     = ["USA"]
  customer_price  = "4.99"
}

data "apple_subscription_price_point_equalizations" "offer" {
  price_point_id = data.apple_subscription_price_points.offer_base.price_points[0].id
}

# Apple refuses a start date earlier than tomorrow and an offer that runs for
# less than three days, so the dates are the caller's to supply.
variable "win_back_starts_on" {
  type        = string
  description = "The first day the offer is shown, YYYY-MM-DD, no earlier than tomorrow."
}

variable "win_back_ends_on" {
  type        = string
  description = "The last day the offer is shown, YYYY-MM-DD, at least two days after it starts."
}

# Half price for three months, for customers who paid for at least six months
# and lapsed between two months and a year ago.
resource "apple_subscription_win_back_offer" "half_price" {
  subscription_id = data.apple_subscriptions.pro_monthly.subscriptions[0].id
  reference_name  = "Pro Monthly win-back 2027"
  # Treat an offer_id as used for good: a replacement offer needs a new one.
  offer_id     = "pro_monthly_winback_2027"
  duration     = "ONE_MONTH"
  offer_mode   = "PAY_AS_YOU_GO"
  period_count = 3

  customer_eligibility_paid_subscription_duration_in_months = 6
  customer_eligibility_time_since_last_subscribed_in_months = { minimum = 2, maximum = 12 }
  customer_eligibility_wait_between_offers_in_months        = 6

  start_date       = var.win_back_starts_on
  end_date         = var.win_back_ends_on
  priority         = "HIGH"
  promotion_intent = "NOT_PROMOTED"

  # Prices cannot change after creation: editing this set replaces the offer.
  prices = concat(
    [{
      territory_id   = "USA"
      price_point_id = data.apple_subscription_price_points.offer_base.price_points[0].id
    }],
    [
      for territory, price_point in data.apple_subscription_price_point_equalizations.offer.price_point_ids : {
        territory_id   = territory
        price_point_id = price_point
      } if territory != "USA"
    ],
  )
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `customer_eligibility_paid_subscription_duration_in_months` (Number) How long a customer must have paid for the subscription before it lapsed to be eligible, in months: any value from `1` to `24`, or `36`, `48` or `60`.
- `customer_eligibility_time_since_last_subscribed_in_months` (Attributes) How long ago the customer's subscription must have lapsed, in months, inclusive at both ends. `{ minimum = 5, maximum = 11 }` shows the offer only to customers lapsed for five to eleven months. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--customer_eligibility_time_since_last_subscribed_in_months))
- `duration` (String) The length of one offer period: `THREE_DAYS`, `ONE_WEEK`, `TWO_WEEKS`, `ONE_MONTH`, `TWO_MONTHS`, `THREE_MONTHS`, `SIX_MONTHS` or `ONE_YEAR`. Changing it forces a new offer.
- `offer_id` (String) The identifier StoreKit transactions and Sales and Trends reports carry for this offer. It must not have been used by another offer in the same subscription group — Apple's documentation adds promotional offers, offer codes and introductory offers to that — and **treat it as reserved once used**: Apple says it must not have *already been used*, not that it must not be in use, so a replacement needs a new one. Changing it forces a new offer.
- `offer_mode` (String) How the customer pays: `PAY_AS_YOU_GO` (the offer price each period for `period_count` periods), `PAY_UP_FRONT` (the offer price once, for the whole duration) or `FREE_TRIAL`. Changing it forces a new offer.
- `period_count` (Number) How many `duration` periods the offer lasts. Changing it forces a new offer.
- `prices` (Attributes Set) The offer price in each storefront it runs in, one per territory. **Changing this destroys the offer and creates a new one**: Apple's update request has no prices, and App Store Connect itself does not allow a price change after creation.

A price is never a number: it references an entry in the subscription's price point catalogue, read through `apple_subscription_price_points`, and `apple_subscription_price_point_equalizations` fans one price out to every territory. For a `FREE_TRIAL` the price still names the storefront the trial runs in. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--prices))
- `priority` (String) How much this offer matters to you, which Apple weighs when choosing between overlapping offers and when ranking it on the App Store: `HIGH` or `NORMAL`.
- `reference_name` (String) The offer's name inside App Store Connect; customers never see it. Must not have been used by another offer of any kind. Changing it forces a new offer.
- `start_date` (String) The first day the offer is available, as a plain `YYYY-MM-DD` date. Apple accepts no earlier than tomorrow, and the exact start time varies by region.
- `subscription_id` (String) The ID of the `apple_subscription` the offer wins customers back to. Changing it forces a new offer. Apple never reports it back — an offer has no subscription relationship — so it is kept as configured.

### Optional

- `customer_eligibility_wait_between_offers_in_months` (Number) How long a customer must wait after this offer ends before they can redeem it again, in months, from `2` to `24`. Omit it for no wait.
- `end_date` (String) The last day the offer is available, as a plain `YYYY-MM-DD` date. Apple requires an offer to run for at least three days. Omit it for an offer with no end date.
- `promotion_intent` (String) Whether to promote the offer on the App Store — on the product page and in editorial and personalized placements: `USE_AUTO_GENERATED_ASSETS` or `NOT_PROMOTED`. Promotion needs an approved subscription image, and replaces any in-app purchase promotions in the same storefront. An unpromoted offer still appears on the Manage Subscriptions page and in the app. Apple's own value is kept when this is omitted.
- `target_subscription_plan_type` (String) Which payment plan the offer applies to, for a subscription sold both ways: `MONTHLY` or `UPFRONT`. Changing it forces a new offer.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Apple's ID for the win-back offer.

<a id="nestedatt--customer_eligibility_time_since_last_subscribed_in_months"></a>
### Nested Schema for `customer_eligibility_time_since_last_subscribed_in_months`

Required:

- `maximum` (Number) The most months since the subscription lapsed, from `1` to `24`, and at least `minimum`.
- `minimum` (Number) The fewest months since the subscription lapsed, from `1` to `24`.


<a id="nestedatt--prices"></a>
### Nested Schema for `prices`

Required:

- `price_point_id` (String) The ID of the subscription price point this price references. It encodes the subscription and the territory, so it is only valid on the subscription it was read from.

Optional:

- `territory_id` (String) The three-letter Apple territory code this price applies to, such as `USA` or `GBR`. Optional: the price point already encodes it, and Apple's own example request does not send it.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Win-back offers import as "<subscription_id>/<offer>", where <offer> is either
# Apple's win-back offer ID or the offer_id.
#
# The subscription ID is required because Apple never reports which
# subscription a win-back offer belongs to.
terraform import apple_subscription_win_back_offer.half_price 6739472901/pro_monthly_winback_2027
```
